cards.explanation: The answer is that the scourge will not touch them. That's the rulers' whole plan. They say, "When the overwhelming scourge passes through it will not touch us…" Then they tell you what they're leaning on: lies and falsehood. Friends, that's an oven mitt made of tissue paper, and nobody wants to be holding the hot pan with that. (Isaiah 28:15)

The answer is Zion. It's right in the verse: "See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation…" The Lord GOD names the place Himself. The rulers picked a hiding place of their own, and He answers with a stone He's laying. (Isaiah 28:16)

The answer is True. The Lord GOD says, "the one who believes will never be shaken." It comes right after the tested stone, the precious cornerstone, the sure foundation. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so believe me, friends, a foundation that doesn't move sounds GOOD. (Isaiah 28:16)

The answer is hail. The Lord GOD says, "Hail will sweep away your refuge of lies, and water will flood your hiding place." So the refuge of lies gets hail and the hiding place gets water. Their hiding place isn't built to hold up against either. (Isaiah 28:17)

The answer is False. The Lord GOD says, "Your covenant with death will be dissolved, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand." That covenant is what the rulers said they had made. He says it comes apart. (Isaiah 28:18)

The answer is trampled. The Lord GOD says, "When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled by it." That's the opposite of what the rulers were counting on. I think this is one of the heavy parts of the passage, so I'll leave it right there. (Isaiah 28:18)

The answer is False. It isn't just one time. The Lord GOD says, "As often as it passes through, it will carry you away; it will sweep through morning after morning, by day and by night." Morning after morning, day and night. It keeps coming back. (Isaiah 28:19)

The answer is strange and disturbing. Isaiah says the LORD will rise up "…to do His work, His strange work, and to perform His task, His disturbing task." Those are the words the text gives. Isaiah doesn't soften them, so I won't either, friends. (Isaiah 28:21)

The answer is that the shackles will become heavier. Isaiah says, "So now, do not mock, or your shackles will become heavier." The mocking makes the shackles weigh more. It's a warning, and it comes with a way out: stop mocking. (Isaiah 28:22)

The answer is that he levels it and then plants. Isaiah says, "When he has leveled its surface, does he not sow caraway and scatter cumin?" The plowing has an end. When the ground is ready, the farmer plants. Work with a finish line, friends. (Isaiah 28:25)

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "He plants wheat in rows and barley in plots, and rye within its border." Rows for the wheat, plots for the barley, a border for the rye. The farmer keeps each crop in its place. (Isaiah 28:25)
The answer is God. Isaiah says, "For his God instructs and teaches him properly." The farmer's know-how comes from God. Isaiah puts the teaching right there in the field. (Isaiah 28:26)

The answer is a stick. Isaiah says, "But caraway is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod." Right before that, he says caraway is not threshed with a sledge. So the sledge stays out of it, and the farmer reaches for a stick. (Isaiah 28:27)

The answer is True. Isaiah says, "Grain for bread must be ground, but it is not endlessly threshed." The farmer threshes it, but not endlessly. I'd be thrilled if my kneading ever came with a stopping point like that, friends. (Isaiah 28:28)

The answer is wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom. Isaiah says, "This also comes from the LORD of Hosts, who is wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom." The farmer's knowing when to plant, when to thresh and when to stop is a picture of that wisdom. The farmer is taught by God, and the wisdom is God's. (Isaiah 28:29)
